title: OpenGDD v0.6 direction file
$comment: An empty direction.json is illegal (SPEC 9.9): a package declares build.direction and carries the 04-presentation.md fence only to say something, and a file that declares nothing says nothing the fence can cite.

semantics.description: SPEC 9.5 self-describing semantics registry. v0.6 defines exactly one tolerance-math id and one metric id; widening either is an additive schema change. Required only when constraints (and so, potentially, thresholds) are present; a direction file with no constraints declares no semantics registry.

pillars.description: SPEC 9.1, keyed by stable id, citable as pillars.<key>

mood.description: SPEC 9.2, keyed by stable local citation id, citable as mood.<key>. Each entry wraps one descriptor:mood:<id> token (SPEC 8a) plus its own viewing binding — two levels of indirection: mood.<key> addresses the citation in this file, descriptor:mood:<id> addresses the descriptor itself, reusable from arbitrary prose.

references.$comment: Every references.<key> entry MUST be cited by at least one judged claim's own optional references field (pillarEntry/antiEntry/mustKeepEntry/moodEntry, all sharing the referencesCite definition). An uncited entry is an orphaned reference and a hard failure. This is a validator-level rule because it requires resolving citations across the document.
references.description: SPEC 9.3, keyed by stable id, citable as references.<key>. Judged claims cite entries through their own references field. The optional REFERENCES section of the direction fence may also cite them as commentary; those fence citations create no completeness or authority rule (SPEC 9.9).

anti.description: SPEC 9.4, keyed by stable id, citable as anti.<key>

constraints.description: SPEC 9.5, keyed by stable id, citable as constraints.colors.<key> / constraints.thresholds.<key> / constraints.timing.<key>. Every entry here is fixed observational checked.

viewing.description: SPEC 9.6, keyed by stable id, citable as viewing.<key>. Referenced by constraints.thresholds.*.viewing and by every judged claim's required viewing field: pillars.*, mood.*, anti.*, must_keep.*.

must_keep.description: SPEC 9.7, keyed by stable id, citable as must_keep.<key>

moodToken.description: SPEC 8a citation grammar: descriptor:<family>:<id>, family fixed to mood in v0.6

packagePath.description: Package-relative path that remains inside the package after normalization (SPEC 1)

mediaFile.description: SPEC 8a media packaging. Byte-signature-matches-declared-format is a validator-level check not expressible over JSON alone. This version defines no numeric media-size conformance limit.

referenceEntry.description: SPEC 9.3 / 8a annotated reference. Annotation presence is inherent in schema validity; property-transfer fidelity is assessed only when a judged claim citing this entry is scored.

criteria.description: Prose statement of the mechanical test (color space/threshold/domain, or an observable element definition). The test's implementation is validator-level (Stage 2/3), not schema-expressible in v0.6.

referencesCite.description: SPEC 9.3/9.10 claim-to-reference edge: the top-level references.<key> entries this claim draws on. Optional — a claim may be judged on its statement/tags alone. Every id MUST resolve to a declared references.<key> entry; a dangling id is a hard failure.

antiEntry.description: SPEC 9.4. Every entry here is judged. observable is optional panel-facing documentation and never changes that. viewing is required and MUST resolve to a declared viewing.<key> entry: the evaluation context the panel scores this claim under. references is the optional claim-to-reference edge.

pillarEntry.description: SPEC 9.1. Every entry here is judged. viewing is required and MUST resolve to a declared viewing.<key> entry. references is the optional claim-to-reference edge.

moodEntry.description: SPEC 9.2/8a. descriptor MUST resolve to a declared descriptors.mood entry. Every entry here is judged: the referenced descriptor's schema-required anti (SPEC 8a) establishes judged status unconditionally. references are optional supplementary evidence, never a precondition. viewing is required and MUST resolve to a declared viewing.<key> entry. references optionally cites top-level references.<key> entries in addition to, never instead of, the descriptor's own references pool (SPEC 8a); the two reference pools are separate and both optional.

scope.description: SPEC 9.5 shared scope shape: applicability domain and proof obligation, per §6's per-sample/aggregate discipline

paletteRef.description: SPEC 9.5 typed palette reference: the palette: prefix, a non-empty palette-key part, a dot, and a non-empty color-name part. The palette key may itself contain dots and a color name may not, so the split point is not textual: the schema carries the alphabet and the validator carries the two-pass resolution that decides where the key ends. The prose spelling palette.<key>.<name> is not accepted here; the JSON channel cites typed, as timing's tuning: key already does.

colorConstraint.description: SPEC 9.5 color constraint: which declared color applies, how close a build must stay to it, and where the claim holds. It carries no hex — color binds one named entry of a declared palette, and a reference that resolves to nothing is a hard failure (validator-level). tolerance: 0 is an exact color pin, verified through its covering acceptance test (SPEC 9.8).

thresholdEntry.$comment: Every element of colors and the single against MUST resolve to a declared, named palette color in manifest.json; a reference that resolves to a palette rather than a color fails as 'names a palette, not a color'. viewing MUST resolve to a declared viewing key; metric MUST appear in semantics.metrics. Package validation MUST also compute the threshold over every (colors element, against) pair at the values the referenced palette colors declare — cross-file, validator-level checks.
thresholdEntry.description: SPEC 9.5 perceptual threshold. Its operands are palette colors, not sibling constraints: a threshold carries its own scope and viewing and is a self-sufficient claim about two declared colors.

timingEntry.description: SPEC 9.5 timing constraint. Carries no numbers; key is a tuning.json reference (SPEC 4a form).

viewingEntry.$comment: judge_qualifications is required (validator-level, not schema-expressible without resolving citations) whenever this entry is cited by a claim whose SPEC 9.3 cultural-source trigger fired.
viewingEntry.description: SPEC 9.6 evaluation-context entry. Structural: inherent in schema validity.

mustKeepEntry.description: SPEC 9.7. may_vary minItems:1 structurally enforces the paint-by-numbers rule. Every entry here is judged; observable is optional documentation only and never changes that. viewing is required. references is the optional claim-to-reference edge.
